deals.notes: Alexander City Marketplace is a 151,843 SF, 100%-leased grocery-anchored community center on 11.55 acres fronting SR-280 (28,429 VPD) in Alexander City, Alabama, built in 1987 and expanded in 1995. Aldi anchors the center in a 47,668 SF box it opened in July 2025 after converting the former Winn-Dixie, which had operated at the site for roughly 30 years, and is joined by Bealls Outlet (28,000 SF), Harbor Freight Tools (17,850 SF), Planet Fitness (13,500 SF) and Dollar Tree (8,300 SF), with a small-shop line of national service and QSR credit that CBRE counts at 82% of effective gross income. In-place base rent from the 9/1/2026 rent roll is $1,357,880, or $8.94 PSF against a CBRE market rent of roughly $13 PSF, and CBRE's in-place pro-forma NOI is $1,283,144 on $1,631,062 of effective gross revenue, a 78.7% margin on a genuinely NNN expense load of $2.29 PSF. Placer.ai data supports the dominance claim: 2 million annual visits, the most-visited shopping center within 10 miles by a 78% margin, and 45% of visitors traveling more than 7 miles, helped by Lake Martin, a 44,000-acre recreation lake 5 miles south that drives seasonal tourism the census rings do not capture. The mark-to-market headline nonetheless overstates capturable upside: the four largest tenants are all materially below market but hold long, cheaply-priced option chains (Aldi flat at $6.94 through February 2055, Harbor Freight to $8.87 through 2052, Bealls to $5.94 through 2042, Planet Fitness to $11.31 through 2046), so that rent is secure, sticky income rather than income a buyer can reset. The genuine underwriting questions are tenant levers and trade-area depth: Bealls can terminate if sales for the year ending January 2028 miss $2,000,000; landlord may recapture roughly 23,800 SF of Aldi's premises after March 2027, cutting about $165,000 of rent or creating a second income stream depending on execution; 29,100 SF rolls between January and April 2027 with Cato at a 16% occupancy cost and Hibbett down 22% since 2022; and population is flat to declining in every ring (16,559 within 5 miles, -0.12% projected annually) even as average household income is forecast to grow 14% by 2030. A Publix sits a half-mile south, so the grocery position is defensible on price point rather than uncontested.
keyAssumptions: SOURCES: roster built from the WHLR MRI rent roll dated 9/1/2026 (authoritative for current tenant, suite, SF, rent, dates and contractual steps) and confirmed line by line against the property OM's site-plan rent roll; options, recovery methods, reported sales and occupancy-cost health ratios from the CBRE Argus In-Place Pro-Forma (identical in the property OM and the FINAL Excel model dated 7/21/2026); 11-year cash flow from the same model; historical income and expense from the WHLR income statement for the 12 months ended December 2025; demographics, traffic count, parking ratio, Placer.ai visitation, shadow outparcels, roof status and competition from the property OM (Project Evergreen_AL_Alex City Marketplace); acreage and portfolio debt context from the Project Evergreen portfolio OM (CBRE, data as of 8/26/2026).

ROSTER TIE-OUT: 20 leases sum to 151,843 SF, exactly the rent roll's stated GLA (0 SF vacant, 100.0% occupied). Monthly base rent sums to $113,156.59, exactly the roll's printed total; annualized = $1,357,879. Monthly expense recoveries sum to $22,667.89, exactly the roll's printed total; annualized = $272,015.

HEADLINE NOI BASIS: noi / effectiveGrossIncome / operatingExpenses are CBRE's published In-Place Pro-Forma for calendar 2027 ($1,631,062 EGR less $347,919 of operating expense = $1,283,144), which is the basis behind the OM's marketed $1,280,000 in-place NOI and which ties EGI - OpEx = NOI.

GPR RECONCILIATION: grossPotentialRent of $1,357,879 is the 9/1/2026 roll's in-place base rent and ties to the roster. CBRE's in-place pro-forma base rent of $1,390,363 is $32,484 higher because it runs contractual rent steps landing during calendar 2027 (Domino's, Advance America, Subway, A's Beauty, Modern Nails, Verizon and Burke's all step up in Dec-2026 through Apr-2027).

ACTUAL vs IN-PLACE: the owner's YE-2025 income statement shows actual NOI of $1,225,391 on $1,627,463 of total income and $402,072 of operating expense. CBRE's $347,919 in-place expense load is normalized — it removes non-recoverable ownership-specific costs (CBRE used a $0.05 PSF assumption) and the $52,485 one-time building painting project in the 2025 actuals, and models management fee at 3.0% of EGR versus the $75,738 cost-reimbursement allocation booked in 2025. Underwrite to the actual expense set if the normalization is not accepted.
NO PRICING: the portfolio is marketed unpriced, so askingPrice, capRate and pricePerSF are null rather than estimated.

ADDRESS: the OM/VDR portfolio table lists 935 Market Place; the CBRE Argus model title page lists 1061 US-280 (the highway the center fronts). Both appear to describe the same site — confirm the deed/tax parcel address before closing.

RONIN SUSHI BAR: the in-place lease runs to 12/31/2026 at $19.00 PSF and is carried at those terms so the roster ties to the roll's base-rent total. The roll's 'New Leases' section and CBRE's model both show a follow-on 5-year term from 1/1/2027 to 12/31/2031; CBRE models it starting at $27.00 PSF with 4% annual increases and describes it as pending. Confirm execution.

TESLA: a 0 SF EV-charging license paying $14,400/year. It is carried as an ordinary tenant (not NAP) because its rent is inside the roll's base-rent total; the owner's income statement books it as 'Parking Rent'.

SALES BASIS: salesPSF and salesYear are the most recent COMPLETE calendar year (2025) from the WHLR 5-year sales history report dated 6/22/2026, verified by dividing reported annual sales by leased SF against the report's own printed PSF. occupancyCost is CBRE's health ratio (total tenant revenue divided by reported sales) from the In-Place Pro-Forma. Anchors (Aldi, Burke's, Harbor Freight, Planet Fitness, Dollar Tree) do not report sales, so those fields are null rather than estimated. Upload the sales report through the app's sales-report import to build the full 2022-2025 trend history.

DEMOGRAPHICS: the OM publishes a 5-mile ring only (16,559 population / $67,900 average household income). The 1- and 3-mile rings and traffic counts are not disclosed in the portfolio book and are left null.

ALDI TENURE - CORRECTION: CBRE's In-Place Pro-Forma shows Aldi's lease start as Jun-1995, which is the ORIGINAL lease inception carried through the Winn-Dixie conversion, NOT Aldi's occupancy. The property OM states Aldi opened in July 2025 and that Winn-Dixie had operated at the center for roughly 30 years beforehand. Aldi has approximately one year of operating history and no reported sales. Do not credit Aldi with 30 years of tenure.

ROSTER CONFIRMED AGAINST THE OM: the property OM's site-plan rent roll matches the 9/1/2026 rent roll on all 19 suites plus the Tesla supercharger for suite, SF, expiry and current rent PSF, and independently confirms both the Ronin Sushi Bar pending 5-year renewal at $27.00 PSF and the Bealls step to $4.91 PSF in February 2027.

DEMOGRAPHICS: the property OM publishes 1-, 3- and 5-mile rings plus a 'True Trade Area'. population3mi / avgHHIncome3mi / medianHHIncome3mi carry the 3-mile figures; the full ring set including the 1-mile and 5-mile rings is stored in marketDemographics. Trade-area figures (32,731 population, $77,491 AHHI) are recorded in the notes rather than a ring field because they are not a fixed radius.

redFlags.description: Burke's Outlet (Bealls Inc.) sales kickout — the 28,000 SF anchor lease (18.4% of GLA, $124,880 of in-place base rent stepping to $137,480 in February 2027) gives the tenant a ONE-TIME right to terminate if sales for the year ending January 2028 do not exceed $2,000,000. Burke's does not report sales in the seller's 5-year report, so the trigger cannot be tested from the data provided. Request Burke's sales history in diligence — this is the single largest single-tenant exposure at the center.

Aldi residual-space recapture — Aldi pays rent on the full 47,668 SF premises ($330,699/yr, 24% of base rent) but operates in only about half of it. Through March 2027 Aldi holds the exclusive right to sublease the roughly 23,800 SF residual; after that, landlord may recapture it on 30 days' notice, at which point Aldi's $6.94 PSF rent and recoveries would apply only to the space it occupies. CBRE has NOT modeled any recapture. A recapture without an immediate backfill would cut roughly $165,000 of base rent and drop occupancy to about 84%.

Near-term anchor and junior-box rollover — 29,100 SF (19.2% of GLA) expires between January and April 2027: Harbor Freight 17,850 SF at $5.50 PSF (4/30/2027), Cato 5,850 SF at $11.00 PSF (1/31/2027) and Hibbett Sports 5,400 SF at $12.00 PSF (1/31/2027). Only Harbor Freight holds options; Cato and Hibbett have none, so 11,250 SF is genuinely at risk within five months of a 2027 closing.

Cato occupancy cost of 16% on declining sales — 2025 sales of $425,632 ($72.76 PSF) are down from $603,344 ($103.14 PSF) in 2023, and CBRE's health ratio of 16% is roughly double a sustainable apparel threshold. The lease expires 1/31/2027 with no options. Treat renewal as unlikely at current rent and underwrite the 5,850 SF as re-leasing exposure, not mark-to-market upside.

Hibbett Sports sales down 22% since 2022 — $878,159 ($162.62 PSF) in 2025 versus $1,123,469 ($208.05 PSF) in 2022, at an 8% occupancy cost, with the lease expiring 1/31/2027 and no renewal options. Combined with Cato, two adjacent junior shops totaling 11,250 SF roll on the same date with deteriorating sales.

Thin trade area — 16,559 people and $67,900 average household income within five miles is well below the portfolio's $87,200 average and limits both rent growth and the depth of replacement-tenant demand. The offsetting factor is genuinely limited competing retail in the market.

Burke's Outlet pays no expense recoveries — the lease has no recovery structure (CBRE recovery type 'None'), so 18.4% of the GLA contributes nothing toward CAM, taxes or insurance. That leakage is already inside the in-place numbers but caps recovery-ratio improvement.

Declining population in every demographic ring - 5-mile population fell from 17,092 (2010) to 16,653 (2020) to 16,559 (2025) and is projected to decline a further 0.12% annually through 2030. The 1-mile ring is shrinking fastest (-0.23% annually). Household income growth (+14% projected to 2030) is the only demographic tailwind. Underwrite rent growth off income, not population, and expect no absorption help from household formation.

Aldi concentration in a store with no operating history - Aldi is 32% of GLA and 25% of total revenue, but the store only opened in July 2025 and has no full year of reported sales. CBRE's model carries the Jun-1995 original lease inception, which can be misread as 30 years of Aldi tenure; the actual operating record is roughly one year. A Publix operates a half-mile south. Request Aldi sales as soon as a full year is available - this is the single largest income concentration at the center.

Bealls Outlet roof is the only one not replaced - all other roofs at the center were replaced between 2023 and 2026, leaving the roof over the 28,000 SF Bealls box (18.4% of building area) as a near-term capital item. It is also the tenant with the sales kickout, so a roof spend may be committed before the termination right is resolved.

Access disruption during the hold-in period - the half-mile bridge connecting SR-63 to US-280 has been closed since May 2025 with completion expected fall 2026. Trailing traffic and sales figures for 2025 and part of 2026 were earned under degraded access, which cuts both ways: it may understate normalized sales, but confirm the completion date rather than assuming the benefit.

upsideItems.detail: Cato ($11.00 PSF) and Hibbett ($12.00 PSF) total 11,250 SF and expire 1/31/2027 with NO renewal options — the only meaningful near-term rent that is genuinely resettable. CBRE marks large shops at $15.00-$18.00 PSF NNN and small shops at $24.00-$27.00 PSF. Re-leasing that space at $15 PSF adds roughly $34,000 of base rent; splitting it into small-shop bays at $24 PSF would add materially more but carries downtime and roughly $15 PSF of TI.

upsideItems.item: Aldi residual space — convert a rent-paying vacancy into a second income stream
upsideItems.detail: Aldi pays on 47,668 SF but uses about half. After March 2027 landlord can recapture roughly 23,800 SF on 30 days' notice. At CBRE's $10.00 PSF NNN anchor market rent that space would generate about $238,000 versus the roughly $165,000 of Aldi rent it currently carries, plus a new recovery-paying tenant. This is a genuine value-creation lever but it is execution-dependent and should be underwritten with downtime, TI and the risk of carrying real vacancy — not booked as automatic upside.

upsideItems.item: Proven re-tenanting track record at the center
upsideItems.detail: Ownership has already backfilled three boxes with better credit and higher rent: Goodies to Burke's Outlet, Factory Connection to Planet Fitness, and Steel's to Harbor Freight. Aldi itself converted the former Winn-Dixie box. That history supports the assumption that the 2027 junior-box roll can be re-leased rather than sitting dark.

All 151,843 SF is leased as of 9/1/2026, so there is no lease-up cost embedded in going-in NOI. CBRE's model still projects 97.5-99.0% economic occupancy across the hold, and excludes Aldi, Burke's, Dollar Tree, Harbor Freight, Planet Fitness and Tesla from the general vacancy factor.

upsideItems.item: Low, stable expense load and recent capital
upsideItems.detail: Operating expenses run $2.29 PSF (CBRE in-place) against $10.79 PSF of effective gross revenue — a 78.7% NOI margin. The majority of roofs are new and the seller completed a $52,485 building repaint in 2025, so near-term capital need is modest.

upsideItems.item: Measured trade-area dominance, not just a marketing claim
upsideItems.detail: Placer.ai shows 2 million annual visits, the most-visited shopping center within 10 miles by a 78% margin over the number two center, and 45% of visitors originating more than 7 miles away. The true trade area is 32,731 people and $77,491 average household income - materially deeper than the 16,559 / $67,900 five-mile ring - and excludes Lake Martin seasonal tourism. No anchor has another same-store location within 25 miles (roughly 30 miles on average), which protects sales from cannibalization.

The SR-63 to US-280 bridge reopens in fall 2026, restoring access that has been degraded since May 2025. Recent and completed area investment includes the Gateway at Lake Martin (2026), a new $97M Benjamin Russell High School campus (2025, 2,300 students), Russell Medical's 81-bed hospital and Central Alabama Community College. Average household income is projected to grow 14% by 2030 against flat population - a spending-power rather than rooftop-growth story.
